::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 15th 1891  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge IV 23
:::

Dear [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd),
I do not suppose the understanding was ever absolutely clear, I have certainly always paid over £20 to [Miss Finlaison](people/person_512.qmd) half in summer and half in winter, and I have, as you say had [£40](organizations/other_160.qmd) in summer, and £50 in winter, but I an impression that I had £10 more for the Christmas number. Indeed I am quite sure that [Mr Smith](people/person_1344.qmd) gave me £10 more for the subeditor, and that I made it £20, £10 being his, and the other £10 from myself[^1]

I began editing the Christmas number for nothing, then he - of his own accord gave me £10 (I believe it was this, but it was often mixed up with payment for writing so that I am not sure[)].

This must be as you please

Yours truly
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: This statement of the way the finances of the [*MP*](organizations/other_52.qmd) worked in the 1880s and 1890s is interesting.  Innes is evidently unwilling to pay the extra £10.
